description: Children with hydranencephaly, whose cerebral cortex was destroyed before birth, were observed by Merker during a week with five families and through some 26,000 messages from caregivers. They were awake and alert, smiled, laughed and cried, built up play sequences with familiar adults, showed preferences, learned simple actions such as kicking trinkets, and had absence seizures that parents recognized as lapses.
limitations: Informal observation, without measures of how much cortical tissue survived, as Watkins and Rees note. Merker 2007 itself is not held here in an open copy, so the passage is cited as Solms quotes it.

sources.quote: They express pleasure by smiling and laughter, and aversion by "fussing," arching of the back and crying (in many gradations), their faces being animated by these emotional states.
